text:
alex.k: hey team :wave: I'm on week 1 and trying to get into the Redwood Console for staging. hit a 403 when opening the feature flags page. Who do I ping to get the right access?
sarah.v: welcome! :tada: did you accept the SSO invite and join the org? sometimes that causes 403s for new users.
alex.k: yes I clicked the invite, signed in with my corp account. I can access the main console but when I go to /console/staging/flags I get `403 Forbidden` and a small UI message: "You don't have permission to view this resource. Contact your admin."
mike.r: hm, that usually means you're missing the ff-staging-operators role (we gate flag write/read there). @infra-ops can you check if alex.k is in the right group?
infra-ops: checking now. please send me the email used to sign up.
alex.k: alex.k@redwood.ai
infra-ops: thanks. I'm seeing a pending invite to the org with limited scopes — looks like an SSO provisioning hiccup. I'll force reprovision and add you to the ff-staging-operators group. give me 5.
console-bot: Note: If console access changes, you'll see an audit event under Console > Admin > Audit Logs. Link: https://console.redwood.internal/admin/audit
sarah.v: if you need temporary read-only access to flags for debugging, you can also use the flags preview endpoint: `GET /api/internal/flags?env=staging&user=alex.k` (requires api token). ping me if you want me to run it.
infra-ops: done — added alex.k to ff-staging-operators and provisioned SSO push. Try again and let me know.
alex.k: trying... still 403 on flags page but can see the list of services. maybe cache?
mike.r: try incognito or clear cookies; SSO sometimes keeps old session. also logout and click the invite link again if prompted.
alex.k: incognito worked! I can now see the staging flags list and toggle sandbox flags (no prod access). thank you. :relieved: Any docs on the flag naming/canary process?
sarah.v: yep — internal doc here: https://docs.redwood.internal/dev/feature-flags (section "Canary & Rollout") — TL;DR: use `staging/` prefix for feature-level flags and attach rollout rule with % traffic. keep experiment flags under `exp/`.
alex.k: perfect. quick question: if I toggle a flag in staging, does it hit Dedicated or Hosted routes? trying to understand infra impact.
mike.r: staging is proxied through our shared dev Dedicated pool for performance tests. toggles are immediate but watch the tracing latency if you flip heavy caches. also don't enable large-batch inferencing flags without a deploy window.
alex.k: noted. last thing — is there a recommended contact for feature flag emergencies?
sarah.v: @infra-ops on-call is the primary; for urgent P1s ping #incidents and add the tag `ff-emergency` so PagerDuty will escalate.
infra-ops: yes, and include a screenshot + approximate user impact and request an emergency rollback if needed.
alex.k: good to know. thanks everyone — appreciate the fast help :thumbsup:
console-bot: Access update: user alex.k was added to group ff-staging-operators by infra-ops at 1798765469.
